speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are experiencing progressive difficulty walking, urinary incontinence, and speech difficulties. To begin our assessment, how long have these symptoms been present, and are they worsening gradually or suddenly?

speaker: Patient
text: 54-year-old male. The patient has been experiencing a gradual difficulty in walking over the past 3 months, requiring wheelchair assistance for the last month. Additionally, there is a history of urinary incontinence for 1 year and recent onset of speech slurring making communication challenging.

speaker: Doctor
text: THAT IS A CONCERNING PROGRESSIVE COURSE. YOU MENTIONED A ONE-YEAR HISTORY OF URINARY INCONTINENCE PRECEDING THE WALKING AND SPEECH ISSUES, WHICH SUGGESTS A SPINAL OR BRAINSTEM PROCESS. HAVE YOU EXPERIENCED ANY NUMBNESS, TINGLING, OR WEAKNESS IN YOUR HANDS OR FEET?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Progressive difficulty walking. I also have Urinary incontinence, Slurred speech, Rigidity in limbs, Mild hand tremor, Orthostatic hypotension.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Multiple System Atrophy (Shy-Drager Syndrome). The combination of autonomic failure (orthostatic hypotension, urinary incontinence), cerebellar signs (gait difficulty, slurred speech), and extrapyramidal features (rigidity, tremor) is classic for this neurodegenerative disorder. I will not proceed with further questioning as the clinical picture is sufficient for a definitive diagnosis.
